Next-Gen 2028 Audi RS6 Avant Getting a US Visa, V8 Power Is Likely – Report
7 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
It’s been more than one and a half years since Audi introduced the latest generation A6. The model was supposed to be christened the A7 as per the brand’s new naming scheme, but the automaker eventually changed its mind.
The reason was that it would have been too confusing for its clientele, though as per the initial plan, Audi was supposed to use even numbers on EVs and odd numbers on ICE-powered cars. And that is precisely why there is no new A4, as the model has become the A5. However, that could change when the mid-cycle refresh arrives, with an obvious emphasis on the word “could,” because the rumor mill hints that the new A5 could be rechristened the A4.
Now, the new-gen Audi A6 may be alive and kicking, but the automaker has yet to introduce its range-topping version. We are talking about the RS 6, which will be offered as a four-door sedan and a five-door station wagon. The former is joining the lineup after a very long wait, because the last RS 6 Sedan was offered for the C6 generation, which was made between 2007 and 2011, based on the VW Group’s C6 platform shared with the lesser S6, A6, and A6 allroad quattro from that era.
The next-generation Audi RS 6 lineup, on the other hand, will utilize the PPC (Premium Platform Combustion. This architecture is the foundation stone not only of the latest A6 family, but also the smaller A5 (B10), and the Mk3 Q5. The new Q7 is also based on this construction, and so is the first-ever Q9, because Audi now has a rival to the likes of the Mercedes GLS, BMW X7, and other full-size crossovers.
Photo: SH Proshots We have seen images of scooped prototypes , which have been joined by all kinds of renderings trying to decipher what it will look like beneath the skin, and it seems that not a single week can usually go by without the next-gen Audi RS 6 making its way to our news feed. The latest information about it came via one of the company’s execs, and it is all about whether the model will reach our shores or not in its long-roof configuration. And the answer is simple: yes!
In a quick sitdown with TheDrive, Audi of America’s Senior Vice President of Product Management, Filip Brabec, was asked whether the all-new Audi RS 6 Avant will come to the United States or not, to which he answered: “If there is globally an RS 6 Avant, then it will come to America.” And there indeed is one, as we have witnessed it multiple times. So, there you have it, folks, official confirmation that the model will take on the likes of the BMW M5 Touring as well on our shores, not only the M5 Sedan.
Its biggest rival in the segment has 717 hp (535 kW /727 ps) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque to play with from its plug-in hybrid 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 engine, enabling 0-60 mph (97 kph) in 3.4 seconds for the Sedan and 3.5 seconds for the Touring. But what exactly will power the all-new Audi RS 6 lineup? Contradicting reports speak about either a V6 or a V8, with electric assistance and twin turbocharging.
If it is the former, then it will likely be the mill used on the new RS 5. And that’s a 2.9-liter twin-turbo V6 making 503 hp (375 kW/510 ps), with the electric motor generating 174 hp (130 kW/177 ps). The total output is rated at 630 hp (470 kW/639 ps), and 0-62 mph (100 kph) is a 3.6-second affair. But if this setup will indeed make its way to the upcoming RS 6, then expect a lot more power, as the model needs to be faster than its predecessor, as it will take an inevitable swing at the BMW M5.
Photo: SH Proshots The previous Audi RS 6 Avant had 621 hp (463 kW/630 ps) to play with from its twin-turbo 4-liter V8, hitting 62 mph (100 kph) in a little over three seconds, and maxing out at 155 mph (250 kph). Some say that a plug-in hybrid V8 could be what powers the upcoming generation, and it could be the setup used on the Bentley Continental GT Speed, which has 771 hp (575 kW/782 ps) available via the right pedal in total.
The quoted outlet expects the all-new Audi RS 6 Avant (and Sedan) to feature a plug-in hybrid V8 assembly, and the model will have a smooth- and quick-shifting eight-speed automatic transmission and the mandatory quattro all-wheel drive system. It will be interesting to learn whether it will indeed be faster than its predecessor, in a straight-line sprint, anyway, because the electric assistance has made it a lot heavier. And let’s not forget than the new BMW M5 is slower than the old one.
Pretty much everything goes at this point when it comes to the performance, as well as the chosen powertrain, and deep down, we hope that the new Audi RS 6 will indeed feature a V8 and not a V6, and that it will be faster than the old one. Everything will be revealed in due course, and we will likely have to wait a few more months before seeing it with no camo in an official environment, as the unveiling should take place in 2027, and the vehicle should go on sale for the 2028 model year in USA.
